prompt: A realistic 1920s photograph on grainy colour film: real people with real skin, pores and stubble. Seen straight down from above, the scene is folded into six mirrored segments round a centre point, as if seen through a brass kaleidoscope, the mirror seams crisp straight lines, each segment the same real photograph repeated so the frame becomes a gold-and-black star. The scene: a hidden underground mint in a speakeasy basement, gangsters in pinstripes working printing presses as sheets of banknotes fly up like confetti, a band in pinstripe suits playing, dancers in fringed dresses, and at the exact centre a tall skinny man in a bowler hat with a heavy gold mayoral chain round his neck, a long narrow face, hollow cheeks and a pencil-thin grey moustache dancing with his arms flung out, while beside every press an exhausted stoker in a soot-black vest sits slumped. Light: hanging brass lamps, the red-hot fireboxes of the presses, strings of bare bulbs; deep shadow between. Plain margins with no writing. Thanks.
